topics.title: Measuring with a book, an eraser or blocks

learn.hook: No ruler? No problem! Measure your table with a book.
points: We can measure length with things like a book, an eraser, a pencil or blocks.
Place the unit end to end with no gaps, and count.
Write what you measured, the unit and the count in a table.
Trace your hand on squared paper. Count the squares from wrist to fingertip to find its length.

example.q: A table is 5 books long. A door is 9 books tall. Which is longer?

learn.reallife: We can measure a mat with a pencil box, or a wall with blocks.

games.title: Measure a bed
games.prompt: Steps to measure a bed with a book
items: Choose a unit, like a book
Put the book at one end
Move it end to end with no gaps

games.title: True or false?
items: We should leave gaps between the books while measuring
Place the books end to end with no gaps.
A longer thing needs more books
We can use an eraser as a unit to measure a pencil box
Any small thing can be a unit.
A bed 12 books long is shorter than a mat 7 books long
12 is more than 7, so the bed is longer.
On squared paper, more squares means a longer hand
Each square is the same size.

quiz.q: Rahul measures his table with a book. It is 5 books long. His bed is 11 books long. Which is longer?
quiz.explain: 11 books is more than 5 books, so the bed is longer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the smaller count is longer

quiz.q: A door is 9 books tall. A cupboard is 7 books tall. How many books taller is the door?
quiz.explain: 9 - 7 = 2 books.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two heights

quiz.q: How should you place the books when you measure?
options: End to end with no gaps
quiz.explain: Gaps would leave parts unmeasured. Place the units end to end.
quiz.mistake: Leaves gaps between units

quiz.q: Isha traces her hand on squared paper. It is 7 squares long. Her brother's is 9 squares long. Whose hand is longer?
quiz.explain: 9 squares is more than 7 squares.
quiz.mistake: Picks the smaller count

quiz.q: A wall is 20 blocks long. Nisha has measured 12 blocks so far. How many more blocks to go?
quiz.explain: 20 - 12 = 8 more blocks.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the gap

quiz.q: Raghav writes in his table: bed 12 books, door 9 books, mat 4 books. Which is the shortest?
quiz.explain: 4 books is the smallest count, so the mat is shortest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest count

teach.ask: Gappu: I have no ruler. How can I measure my bed?
teach.praise: Yes! Use a book, put it end to end with no gaps and count.
teach.nudge: What can I use instead of a ruler? How do I place it?

learn.hook: Late for school! Which path will get you there fastest?
points: There can be many paths between two places.
The shortest path is the quickest to walk.
The longest path takes the most time.
To compare paths, count the boxes or steps along each one.
A straight path between two points is the shortest.

example.q: Path A to school has 8 boxes. Path B has 5 boxes. Path C has 11 boxes. Which is shortest and which is longest?
steps: 5 is the least and 11 is the most.
example.answer: B is shortest, C is longest

learn.reallife: Auto drivers pick short routes to save time and fuel.

games.title: Path lengths
games.prompt: From the shortest path to the longest

games.title: True or false?
items: The shortest path takes the least time to walk
A curvy path is shorter than a straight path between the same two points
The straight path is the shortest.
We can compare paths by counting boxes along them
More boxes means a longer path.
The longest path is the quickest
A path of 6 boxes is longer than a path of 9 boxes

quiz.q: Path A to school is 8 boxes long. Path B is 5 boxes long. Which path is shorter?
quiz.explain: 5 boxes is less than 8 boxes, so Path B is shorter.
quiz.mistake: Picks the bigger number as shorter

quiz.q: Path X is 12 boxes, Path Y is 9 boxes and Path Z is 15 boxes. Which is the longest?
quiz.explain: 15 is the biggest number, so Path Z is the longest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the shortest path

quiz.q: Ravi takes a 7-box path. Gita takes a 10-box path. How many more boxes does Gita walk?
quiz.explain: 10 - 7 = 3 more boxes.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two paths

quiz.q: You want to reach the shop quickly. Which path should you take?
quiz.explain: The shortest path takes the least time.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a longer path is faster

quiz.q: Which line between two dots is the shortest?
quiz.explain: A straight line goes directly, so it is the shortest way.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a curved line is shorter

quiz.q: Meena walks 6 boxes to the park, then 4 more boxes to school. Arjun's path to school is 8 boxes. Whose path is shorter?
quiz.explain: Meena walks 6 + 4 = 10 boxes. 8 is less than 10, so Arjun's is shorter.
quiz.mistake: Compares only part of Meena's path

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find the shortest path to school?
teach.praise: Yes! Count the boxes on each path and pick the one with the fewest.
teach.nudge: How can I compare the paths? Which one should I choose?

learn.hook: A giraffe is so tall! How many blocks tall is it?
points: We can measure heights with blocks stacked one on another.
A giraffe is 9 blocks tall, a camel 7 blocks and a monkey 2 blocks.
The one with more blocks is taller. The one with fewer blocks is shorter.
The tallest has the most blocks. The shortest has the fewest.

example.q: Giraffe 9 blocks, camel 7 blocks, monkey 2 blocks. Which is the tallest and which is the shortest?
example.answer: Giraffe is tallest, monkey is shortest

learn.reallife: In the school assembly, children stand in lines from shortest to tallest.

quiz.q: A giraffe is 9 blocks tall. A camel is 7 blocks tall. Which is taller?
quiz.explain: 9 blocks is more than 7 blocks.
quiz.mistake: Picks the smaller number

quiz.q: How many blocks taller is a 9-block giraffe than a 7-block camel?
quiz.explain: 9 - 7 = 2 blocks.
quiz.mistake: Adds the heights

quiz.q: A monkey is 2 blocks, a goat 3 blocks and a camel 7 blocks tall. Which is the shortest?
quiz.explain: 2 is the fewest blocks, so the monkey is shortest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the tallest

quiz.q: The camel is 7 blocks tall. The monkey is 2 blocks tall. How many blocks taller is the camel?
quiz.explain: 7 - 2 = 5 blocks.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away

quiz.q: A horse is 6 blocks tall. A camel is 7 blocks tall. Is the horse taller or shorter?
quiz.explain: 6 is less than 7, so the horse is shorter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a big animal is always taller

quiz.q: A 2-block monkey sits on top of a 7-block camel. How many blocks tall are they together?
quiz.explain: Stack the heights: 7 + 2 = 9 blocks.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know which animal is the tallest?
teach.praise: Yes! Count the blocks. The one with the most blocks is tallest.
teach.nudge: How can I measure them? Which count wins?

learn.hook: How long is your table? You can measure it with your own hand!
points: A hand-span goes from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger. Spread the hand wide.
We measure small things like a table with hand-spans.
We measure big things like a room with steps.
Longer things need more spans or steps.
People get different answers. A bigger hand needs fewer spans.

example.q: Riya's table is 6 of her hand-spans long. Her father's hand is bigger. Will he count more or fewer spans?
steps: Father's span is longer than Riya's.
Each long span covers more of the table.

learn.reallife: In gully cricket, children measure the pitch with steps. Tailors and carpenters measure too.

games.title: True or false?
items: A room is easier to measure in steps than in hand-spans.
A room is big. Steps are longer, so we count fewer.
Everyone's hand-span is the same size.
Hands are different sizes, so spans are different too.
With the same hand, a longer thing needs more hand-spans.
More length to cover means more spans.
A big hand needs more spans than a small hand for the same table.
A big span covers more, so it needs fewer spans.
We spread the hand wide to make a hand-span.
A span goes from the thumb tip to the little finger tip.

quiz.q: Arjun's book is 2 hand-spans long. His table is 7 hand-spans long. Which is longer?
quiz.explain: The table needs 7 spans and the book needs only 2. More spans means longer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a smaller number of spans means longer

quiz.q: Meena's mat is 5 spans long. Her rope is 9 spans long. How many spans longer is the rope?
quiz.explain: Find the difference. 9 − 5 = 4. The rope is 4 spans longer.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two lengths instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: What is the best way to measure the length of your classroom?
quiz.explain: A classroom is big. Steps are long, so counting is quick.
quiz.mistake: Picks a small unit that takes too long for a big room

quiz.q: Kabir walks across a room in 12 steps. His dad does it in 8 steps. Why?
quiz.explain: Dad's steps are longer. Longer steps cover the room in fewer steps.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the room changed size

quiz.q: A table is 4 hand-spans long. Two such tables are put end to end. How many hand-spans long are they?
quiz.explain: Each table is 4 spans. 4 + 4 = 8 spans.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one table

quiz.q: Harpreet walks 6 steps to the door and 6 more steps to the gate. How many steps in all?
quiz.explain: Add the two parts. 6 + 6 = 12 steps.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one part of the walk

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I measure my table without a ruler?
teach.praise: Great idea! I will put my hand-span again and again and count. No ruler needed!
teach.nudge: What part of my body can I use? What do I do after I place it?

learn.hook: A pillow is big but light. A small stone is heavy! Size does not always tell weight.
points: Hold one thing in each hand. Feel which one pulls down more. That is heavier.
On a balance or a see-saw, the heavier side goes down.
The lighter side goes up.
A big thing is not always heavy. A balloon is big but light.

example.q: On a balance, a bag of rice goes down. A bag of puffed rice goes up. Which is heavier?

learn.reallife: The vegetable seller weighs onions on a balance. On a see-saw, the heavier child goes down.

quiz.q: Which one is the heaviest?
quiz.explain: A brick is hard and solid. It is much heavier than a feather or a leaf.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how things feel when we lift them

quiz.q: On a see-saw, Arjun goes down and Riya goes up. Who is heavier?
quiz.explain: The heavier side of a see-saw goes down. Arjun went down.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the side that goes up is heavier

quiz.q: A big balloon and a small stone. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: The balloon is full of air and is very light. The small stone is heavier.
quiz.mistake: Thinks bigger things are always heavier

quiz.q: On a balance, 1 melon weighs the same as 6 apples. 2 such melons weigh the same as how many apples?
quiz.explain: Each melon is 6 apples. 2 melons are 6 + 6 = 12 apples.
quiz.mistake: Forgets there are 2 melons

quiz.q: A pencil balances 3 ₹1 coins. A pen balances 5 ₹1 coins. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: The pen needs 5 coins to balance. 5 is more than 3, so the pen is heavier.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fewer coins means heavier

quiz.q: A bag of onions balances 10 blocks. A bag of potatoes balances 14 blocks. How many more blocks for the potatoes?
quiz.explain: Find the difference. 14 − 10 = 4 more blocks.
quiz.mistake: Adds the blocks instead of finding the difference

teach.ask: Gappu: My balloon is big. So it must be heavy, right?
teach.praise: Oh! Big things can be light. I should lift them or use a balance to check.
teach.nudge: Is a big thing always heavy? How can I check which is heavier?

learn.hook: Lift your school bag, then an eraser. Which one pulls your hand down more?
points: Use 'heavier than' and 'lighter than' to compare two things.
A sheet of paper is lighter than an eraser. A bag of books is heavier than a pencil box.
Arrange things from lightest to heaviest. This is increasing order of weight.
Lift two things, one in each hand, to guess which is heavier.

example.q: Arrange from lightest to heaviest: school bag, paper, eraser, pencil box.
steps: Then the eraser, then the pencil box.
The school bag is the heaviest.
example.answer: Paper, eraser, pencil box, school bag

learn.reallife: At the railway station, luggage is weighed to see how heavy it is.

items.text: An eraser is ___ than a school bag
A pumpkin is ___ than a tomato
A feather is ___ than a stone
A full water bottle is ___ than an empty one

quiz.q: Fill in: A sheet of paper is ___ an eraser.
quiz.explain: A sheet of paper is thin and light. An eraser is a little heavier.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up heavier and lighter

quiz.q: Which is the heaviest: paper, eraser, pencil box or school bag?
quiz.explain: A school bag full of books is the heaviest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the lightest thing

quiz.q: Which list goes from lightest to heaviest?
options: School bag, pencil box, eraser, paper
Eraser, paper, school bag, pencil box
Paper, eraser, pencil box, school bag
quiz.explain: It starts with the lightest, paper, and ends with the heaviest, the school bag.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the order

quiz.q: Tanvi holds a ball of cotton in one hand and an orange in the other. Which hand feels heavier?
quiz.explain: An orange is heavier than a small ball of cotton, so that hand is pulled down more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks soft and fluffy means heavy

quiz.q: Fill in: A big pumpkin is ___ a small lemon.
quiz.explain: A big pumpkin weighs much more than a small lemon.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up heavier and lighter

quiz.q: Which of these is the lightest?
quiz.explain: A leaf weighs very little. The others are much heavier.
quiz.mistake: Picks a heavy object

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I tell which is heavier without a balance?
teach.praise: Yes! Lift one in each hand. The heavier one pulls your hand down more.
teach.nudge: What can I do with my hands to compare?

learn.hook: A see-saw is a balance! The heavier friend goes down.
points: On a balance, the heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up.
If both sides are level, the things weigh the same.
A bag of sand is heavier than a bag of dry leaves of the same size.
Shops use a pan balance or a weighing machine. We check our own weight on a weighing machine.

example.q: A balance has a bag of sand on one side and a same-size bag of dry leaves on the other. Which side goes down?
steps: Sand is packed tight and heavy.

learn.reallife: The vegetable seller weighs potatoes on a pan balance or a weighing machine.

games.title: True or false?
items: On a balance, the heavier side goes up
If both pans are level, the things weigh the same
A bag of sand is heavier than a same-size bag of dry leaves
Sand weighs much more than leaves.
We can check our weight on a weighing machine
Weighing machines are at homes, clinics and stations.
A bigger bag is always heavier
A big bag of leaves can be lighter than a small bag of sand.

quiz.q: On a balance, the left pan goes down and the right pan goes up. Which side is heavier?
quiz.explain: The heavier side always goes down.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the side that goes up is heavier

quiz.q: A bag of sand and a bag of dry leaves are the same size. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: Same size does not mean same weight. Sand is much heavier.
quiz.mistake: Thinks same size means same weight

quiz.q: Both pans of a balance are level. What does it tell us?
quiz.explain: When the pans are level, the two sides weigh the same.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a level balance means

quiz.q: On a balance, a brick goes down and a sponge goes up. How should you mark the sponge?
quiz.explain: The sponge went up, so it is the lighter one.
quiz.mistake: Marks the side that went up as heavy

quiz.q: Where can you check your own weight?
quiz.explain: A weighing machine shows how heavy we are.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up tools for length, time and weight

quiz.q: Ramu weighs 25 kg. His father weighs 70 kg. How much heavier is his father?
quiz.explain: 70 - 25 = 45. His father is 45 kg heavier.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two weights

teach.ask: Gappu: On a balance, which side goes down?
teach.praise: Right! The heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up.
teach.nudge: Does the heavy side go up or down?

learn.hook: Let us make nimbu pani! How many spoons of sugar for each glass?
points: For 1 glass of lemonade: 1 glass of water, 2 spoons of sugar and 1 spoon of lemon juice.
For 2 glasses, take twice as much: 2 glasses of water, 4 spoons of sugar, 2 spoons of lemon juice.
For more glasses, add the amounts for 1 glass again and again.
Fill bottles using the same glass to see whose bottle holds more, less or the same.

example.q: One glass of lemonade needs 2 spoons of sugar. How many spoons for 4 glasses?

learn.reallife: In summer, families make nimbu pani for guests.

items.q: Lemon juice for 5 glasses, 1 spoon each
Water for 4 glasses of lemonade, 1 glass each

quiz.q: One glass of lemonade needs 2 spoons of sugar. How many spoons for 3 glasses?
quiz.explain: 2 spoons for each glass: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 3

quiz.q: One glass needs 1 spoon of lemon juice. How many spoons for 4 glasses?
quiz.explain: 1 spoon for each of 4 glasses is 4 spoons.
quiz.mistake: Uses the amount for only one glass

quiz.q: Riya used 10 spoons of sugar, 2 spoons for each glass. How many glasses did she make?
quiz.explain: Count in 2s to 10: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. That is 5 glasses.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of spoons

quiz.q: Tina's bottle fills 5 glasses. Om's bottle also fills 5 glasses. Which is true?
quiz.explain: Both fill 5 of the same glass, so they hold the same amount.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two bottles can never hold the same

quiz.q: Anu's bottle fills 7 glasses. Raj's bottle fills 4 glasses. How many more glasses does Anu's hold?
quiz.explain: 7 - 4 = 3 glasses more.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two amounts

quiz.q: Ben's bottle fills 3 glasses, Sia's fills 6 and Lali's fills 4. Whose bottle holds the least?
quiz.explain: 3 glasses is the smallest amount.
quiz.mistake: Picks the bottle that holds the most

teach.ask: Gappu: I know how to make 1 glass of lemonade. How do I make 2 glasses?
teach.praise: Yes! Take twice the water, sugar and lemon juice.
teach.nudge: Should I use the same amounts or more for 2 glasses?

learn.hook: A bucket, a jug and a glass. Which one holds the most water?
points: Capacity means how much a thing can hold.
A bucket holds more water than a glass.
We can measure with a cup: how many cups fill the jug?
The one that needs more cups to fill holds more.
A tall thing does not always hold more. Pour and check.

example.q: A jug fills 5 glasses. A bottle fills 3 glasses. Which holds more?

learn.reallife: Mummy uses a cup to measure water for rice. Milk comes in packets and bottles.

games.title: Holds least to most
games.prompt: Holds the least water to holds the most

quiz.q: Which one holds the most water?
quiz.explain: A bucket is much bigger inside. It can fill many cups.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how much fits inside

quiz.q: A jug fills 6 glasses. A bottle fills 4 glasses. How many more glasses does the jug fill?
quiz.explain: Find the difference. 6 − 4 = 2 more glasses.
quiz.mistake: Adds the glasses instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: A pot fills 3 jugs. Each jug fills 5 glasses. How many glasses does the pot fill?
quiz.explain: 3 jugs of 5 glasses each. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 5 instead of counting 3 groups of 5

quiz.q: Using the same cup, Kabir fills his bottle with 4 cups. Joseph fills his with 7 cups. Whose bottle holds more?
quiz.explain: Joseph's bottle takes 7 cups. 7 is more than 4, so it holds more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fewer cups means it holds more

quiz.q: What does capacity mean?
options: How much a thing can hold
quiz.explain: Capacity tells how much water, milk or sand a thing can hold.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up capacity with weight or length

quiz.q: A bucket holds 10 mugs of water. Meena has poured in 6 mugs. How many more mugs to fill it?
quiz.explain: Count up from 6 to 10: 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 4 more mugs.
quiz.mistake: Adds the mugs instead of finding what is missing

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I find which bottle holds more water?
teach.praise: Yes! Fill each one with cups and count. More cups means it holds more!
teach.nudge: What can I pour with? What do I count?
